activity_context.topic_title: Cumulative Distribution Functions for Discrete Random Variables

feedback.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(X\ge 6).$

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ | $0.8$ | $1.0$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

$$
P(X>a)=1-P(X\le a)=1-F(a).
$$

Here, we want to compute $P(X\ge 6).$ However, this interval is stated in the form $X\ge 6,$ not $X>6.$

So first, we must convert the interval $X\ge 6$ to the form $X>a.$ Looking at the given possible values of $X,$ we see that $X\ge 6$ is equivalent to $X>4.$

Therefore, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & =P(X>4) \\  & =1-P(X\le 4) \\  & =1-F(4) \\  & =1-0.3 \\  & =0.7.\end{aligned}
$$
